issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s deposit of rent in court may be treated as payment to the landlord when physical tender is impracticable and the statutory conditions for deposit are met, but a court deposit is not automatically sufficient.
material_facts: The tenant and landlady had extremely strained relations, including criminal proceedings, and lived in adjacent premises.
The tenant regularly deposited rent in court rather than paying it directly to the landlady.
The lower courts held that the deposits did not amount to payment to the landlady, but did not consider whether other means of direct payment were practicable or had been refused.
issues.conclusion: The lower courts construed the deposit provisions too narrowly. Because they had not considered whether the circumstances justified court deposits after accounting for other possible means of payment, the finding was set aside and the case remanded for that determination. If no circumstance justifying court deposit was established, the eviction decree would stand; otherwise, the eviction petition would be dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3(1)(a), 7-C(1) and 7-C(6) of the United Provinces (Temporary) Control of Rent and Eviction Act, 1947, the expression concerning rent paid to the landlord must be construed liberally and in light of the parties’ circumstances. Physical, person-to-person tender is not required where it is impracticable; payment may be attempted by money order, messenger, or by asking the landlord to nominate a bank account. A court deposit is permissible where the landlord refuses rent tendered through such means, and a deposit made in accordance with Section 7-C(1) is deemed duly paid under Section 7-C(6). A tenant may not, however, deposit rent in court without meeting the statutory conditions. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.arrears_eviction_proceeding: The landlord sought eviction on the ground that rent was in arrears.
predicates.relationship_makes_physical_tender_impra: The tenant and landlord had relations so strained that physically tendering rent to the landlord was impracticable.
predicates.tenant_regularly_deposited_rent_in_court: The tenant regularly placed the rent in court instead of paying it directly to the landlord.
predicates.lower_courts_did_not_assess_alternative_: The lower courts did not determine whether other ways of paying rent were available or whether the landlord had refused payment through those means.
predicates.case_remanded_for_assessment_of_whether_: The case is sent back for a determination of whether the circumstances justified depositing the rent in court.

issues.definition: When an arrears-based eviction case involves impracticable physical tender, regular court deposits, and no lower-court assessment of alternative payment methods, the case is sent back to determine whether the deposits were justified.
